records.name: Saint Peter's Episcopal Church
records.summary: An Episcopal parish at Third and Pine streets with a food cupboard open Saturday mornings. No eligibility rules are listed, and the choir welcomes amateur and skilled singers.
records.what_you_do: Get food at the Saturday morning cupboard, sign up to volunteer there, sing with the choir on Sunday mornings, or join one of the church's groups, such as the churchyard gardeners or the book group.

schedule.text: Food cupboard on Saturday mornings, with donations taken from 8 to 10 am. Sunday services at 9 am (family and spoken) and 11 am (choral with organ). Choir rehearses Sundays from 9:30 to 10:45 am.

locations.label: Church, across from the Parish House

cost.text: The food cupboard is free, per the PA 211 listing and the parish food cupboard page

access.notes: Ushers will help families with strollers, per the FAQ.

first_step.how: Come to the 11 am Sunday service, or fill out the parish online welcome form and the parish will add you to its email list.
first_step.basis: The parish has an online welcome form and holds a Welcome Coffee and Conversation several times a year, and its FAQ says you do not need to be Episcopalian to attend.
first_step.what_to_expect: The 11 am service has the choir and organ, and there are 9 am family and spoken services as well. The FAQ describes readings and a sermon, then Communion, and it does not say how long a service runs. Dress is up to you, and children are invited to join in. The site lists no cost for worship.
first_visit_tips: On Sundays, park in the church lot at 315 Lombard Street, and move your car after the service because the lot locks on Sunday afternoons.
SEPTA bus routes 12, 40 and 57 stop at the church.
Call the parish office at 215-925-5968 on a weekday, 8:30 am to 4 pm, with questions.

records.notes: The parish food cupboard page says food is handed out on Saturday mornings and that donations are taken from 8 to 10 am, so the 8 to 10 am window is the donation time. Tier 1 listed the church at 313 Pine Street, which is the Parish House; both addresses are now shown. The site has no accessibility page, so wheelchair access, ASL and elevators are not stated. The FAQ names SEPTA bus routes but no stop, so nearest_septa is left out. The food cupboard serves about 80 families a week, per the page.

records.name: Saints United Lutheran Church
records.summary: A Lutheran congregation on Ryan Avenue in the Northeast with Sunday worship at 10 am, in person and online. Its site has a worship bulletin dated October 2026.
records.what_you_do: Come to Sunday worship at 10 am, in person or online. The church also runs three outreach ministries: Feed the Hungry (members make casseroles and bagged sandwiches), Feast of Justice (food gifts for families), and Aid for Friends (cooking meals for homebound older adults). The site does not say how to join them.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 10 am, in person and online.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 10 am, or watch the live service on the church's YouTube or Facebook page first.
first_step.basis: The site invites questions and has a contact form, but it describes no newcomer program or welcome class.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe what a first visit is like, how long the service runs, or whether there is a children's program. The Sunday service is at 10 am and is streamed live, so you can watch it before you go.
first_visit_tips: Watch a Sunday service online first to get a feel for the church.
Send questions through the contact form, or call 215-624-6446 before you come.

records.notes: The site has no welcome, newcomer, events or accessibility page. The Our Church Programs page names a council (third Thursday), a women's group (second Tuesday) and a worship and music group (second Thursday) with no join details, so they are left out of the record. The bulletin file name says 18th Sunday after Pentecost, but the post title says 19th; check before quoting it. The contact form asks for a recipient, name, email, phone, subject and message, and a CAPTCHA. Tier 1 said the outreach was not on the site, so it is new here. Feast of Justice's own site lists locations on Tyson Ave and Castor Ave, which does not match the church page's account of St. John's Lutheran; use the group's own site for locations.

records.name: Salt and Light Community Church
records.summary: A church with two Philadelphia locations, Southwest and Mount Airy, with Sunday services, family Bible study, and food giveaways.
records.what_you_do: Join Sunday worship, a family Bible study on Wednesday evenings or Friday afternoons, or help with the food giveaway on Saturday mornings or the holiday giveaway.

schedule.text: Sunday services at 8 am in Mount Airy and at 9:30 am and 11:30 am in Southwest. Family Bible study on Wednesdays at 7 pm (Southwest) and Fridays at 1:30 pm (Mount Airy). The church calendar also lists other weekly groups on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Thursdays and Fridays, a community meal on Wednesdays at 5:30 pm, and a food giveaway on Saturdays at 9:30 am.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at either location: Mount Airy at 8 am, or Southwest at 9:30 or 11:30 am.
first_step.basis: The church has a New Members class and a page that lists next steps, and Sunday worship is open to the public. The site does not say whether visitors may sit in on the class.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not say how long a Sunday service runs or describe a greeting for visitors. The site lists no cost for worship or for the groups it names.
first_visit_tips: Check the address before you go, since the Mount Airy map link points to a different place than the street address on the site.
Watch past services on the church's YouTube channel to see what worship is like.

records.notes: Two address problems to check before a visit: the Mount Airy map link points to 915 E. Gowen Ave, and its Get Here link searches for a seminary chapel, while the site gives 7301 Germantown Ave. The Southwest footer shows ZIP 19142 but the location block gives 19143. The calendar lists weekly groups with no places or dates, and it lists a Saturday 9:30 am food giveaway; the site's video is for a holiday giveaway, so confirm the Saturday giveaway before sending people. Bethesda's Pool, a counseling and wellness ministry on the church site, was not checked and is not in this record. The live page shows an Oct 7, 2026 livestream thumbnail, which moves the last sign of life to 2026-10.

records.name: Sanctuary Fellowship Worship Center
records.summary: A non-denominational, Bible-teaching church on North 42nd Street with women's and men's fellowship groups and outreach that includes clothing giveaways and volunteering at its Safe House Pantry.
records.what_you_do: Join the Women's or Men's Fellowship for Bible teaching and fellowship, help with clothing and household giveaways or the Safe House Pantry, or give through the donate button on the site.

first_step.how: Call 1-800-543-5244 or email sfwcenter@gmail.com to ask about worship times and how to join a fellowship group.
first_step.basis: The homepage welcomes visitors and gives a phone number, an email address and a contact form, and it describes fellowship groups. It publishes no service times or newcomer program.
first_visit_tips: Call or email before your first visit, because the website does not publish service times.

records.notes: The site gives no service times, Bible study times or visit details. One web search found only old Northeast Times church listings (2012 to 2020) that do not include this church, so service times are still unknown. The homepage footer reads 2020 and no dated news appears, so probably_active rests on the working site and on the church appearing in the July 2026 IRS e-Postcard dataset, not on dated news. Women's and men's fellowship and the Safe House Pantry are confirmed on the homepage, not on the ministries page. The site does not say whether the Safe House Pantry gives food, household goods or both.

records.name: Save Cambodia
records.summary: A nonprofit advocacy group that aims to unite Cambodians around the world and push for accountability and reform in Cambodia, through volunteer reporting, campaigns and advocacy at the United Nations.
records.what_you_do: Sign up on the Join Now page to get its news and urgent alerts, watch or join its community briefings (mostly online), and take action by writing letters when it asks.

schedule.text: Community briefings and discussions are listed on the group's calendar, usually on Saturday afternoons and often held online.

locations.label: Mailing address (PO box, no meetings published)

cost.text: No fee is listed on the join page

access.notes: Several listed briefings are in Khmer, and some stream live on YouTube.

first_step.how: Sign up on the Join Now page with your first name, last name and email, then watch the calendar for the next online briefing.
first_step.basis: The join form and the public calendar are open to anyone, but the site does not describe a volunteer orientation or a welcome for new members.
first_step.what_to_expect: Briefings on the calendar usually run about an hour to an hour and a half, often on a Saturday afternoon, and many are held online in Khmer. The join form asks only for a name and an email address, and no fee is listed. The site does not describe any volunteer training.
first_visit_tips: Check the language on each calendar entry, since many briefings are in Khmer.
Look for the YouTube link on the event listing, since some briefings stream live there.
Most in-person events on the calendar were held out of state or abroad, so online is the usual way to take part.

records.notes: Scope question for the reviewer: the only Philadelphia link is a PO box in the footer, and the briefings are online or held out of state or abroad, while the work is national and international. Consider out_of_area. I kept publish from tier 1. The join form shows a notice that it still needs a storage location, so a sign-up may not go through; check it before sending people there. I removed a dated sentence from schedule.text (the April 2026 briefing), and the 2026 dates now sit in last_sign_of_life. The 2026-08 sign of life is the August 2026 urgent alerts on the homepage.

records.name: Save the Academy Coalition
records.summary: Volunteers working to keep the public museum of the Academy of Natural Sciences open on the Parkway. The museum's public doors closed on September 27, 2026, and the campaign is pressing officials to change that decision.
records.what_you_do: Sign the petition, contact city and state officials, make flyers, collect personal stories, and join volunteer work for rallies, vigils and events.

schedule.text: No regular meeting is listed. Rallies, vigils and hearings are one time events announced on the campaign site.

locations.label: Academy of Natural Sciences museum (campaign focus)

cost.text: Free to join. Donations are optional and go through the campaign's fiscal sponsor, the Center for Philadelphia's Urban Future.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer form linked from the campaign homepage, or sign the petition.
first_step.basis: The volunteer form and the public events are open to anyone, and the page describes no training or application.
first_step.what_to_expect: The campaign lists public events such as rallies, vigils and City Council hearings on its site. Volunteer work includes writing to officials, making flyers, collecting personal stories, and asking groups to speak up. Replies can be slow because volunteers run the campaign.
first_visit_tips: The next City Council hearing is Monday, October 26, 2026, at 2 pm. The site does not list its location in the text, so check the events section first.
Follow the campaign on Instagram for updates.

records.notes: Tier 1 said the year was missing for the council hearing. The site now gives Monday, October 26, 2026, at 2 pm, moved from October 7, and that date sits in tips, not in schedule text. The hearing location is not in the page text. The site and its news page both say the public museum closed on September 27, 2026. Partner organizations named on the events section are Philly Science Action, Green Philly and Skype a Scientist (hosts of the September 8, 2026 rally), and the Center for Philadelphia's Urban Future (fiscal sponsor). The campaign site gives no links for the first three, so they stay in leads_only without a usable link.

records.name: Schuylkill Dragons
records.summary: A women's dragon boat team founded in 2001 that paddles on the Schuylkill River and trains year round, with paddlers from their 20s to their 80s.
records.what_you_do: Take the five-week Intro to Paddling class in late spring. If invited to the team, join practices on the water and winter workouts.

schedule.text: Practices from April to October on Tuesdays and Thursdays from about 6:15 to 7:30 pm and Saturdays from 9 to 10 am, with early Wednesday mornings added in midsummer. The five-week beginner class meets on Sunday evenings, usually late May through June. From November to March the team holds weekly group weight training and rowing machine sessions, and indoor paddling on Saturdays from January to March.

locations.label: Dragon boat dock, West Fairmount Park

cost.text: $150 for the five-week Intro to Paddling class. If you are invited to join the team, yearly dues are prorated, and festival costs are billed separately at the end of the season.

requirements.gear: Life jackets and paddles are provided for the class. A seat cushion is suggested, such as a square of yoga mat.

first_step.how: Join the mailing list on the Join Us page, then register for the Intro to Paddling class when registration opens, usually in April.
first_step.basis: No experience is needed, the team runs a five-week beginner class, and the site gives a clear sign-up step. Joining the team itself is by invitation after the class.
first_step.what_to_expect: The five-week class meets on Sunday evenings, usually from late May through June. Coaches assess students during the course, and invitations to join the team go out after it ends. Life jackets and paddles are provided, and the class costs $150.
first_visit_tips: Bring a seat cushion, since the page suggests one to help prevent blisters.
Watch the team's Instagram and Facebook accounts for the day registration opens, usually in April.
Once you join, members are encouraged to come to at least two practices a week.

records.notes: The site gives no dock directions, parking or accessibility details for the dock. The 20s to 80s age range is carried over from tier 1; the pages read in this pass say only women of all ages, with no range. The homepage has a 2026 Race Calendar heading with no events listed, so there is no dated evidence beyond the site itself, and probably_active stays. Board members listed with 2021 and 2023 are not counted as evidence of activity.

notes: Budget: 1 of 1 WebSearch used; 36 WebFetch calls, including 2 failed attempts at aidforfriends.org. Corrections to tier 1: (1) Saint Peter's: the church and the Parish House are separate addresses, so both are listed, and the food cupboard page gives 8 to 10 am as the donation window with distribution on Saturday mornings. (2) Salt and Light: an Oct 7, 2026 livestream moves the last sign of life to 2026-10, and the calendar lists a weekly Saturday food giveaway. (3) Save the Academy: the hearing has a year on the site now (Oct 26, 2026), and the schedule text no longer carries a dated event. (4) Save Cambodia: a dated sentence was removed from schedule.text. (5) Sanctuary: the homepage confirms the women's and men's fellowships, the Safe House Pantry and giveaways, but no service times appear anywhere on the site, and the search found nothing reliable. Verdicts: 7 publish, 0 hide, 0 not_a_group, 0 duplicate, 0 out_of_area. Reviewer flags: Save Cambodia's only Philadelphia link is a PO box, so out_of_area is worth considering; Sanctuary's status is probably_active on a working site and an IRS listing, not dated news, so confidence is low. Partner organizations were left in leads_only because the tier 2 brief routes partners there. Feast of Justice was fetched and left as a lead; Aid for Friends was unreachable; the three Save the Academy partners have no usable link on the campaign site. No rate limiting was seen, and no other pages were blocked.
